about: The last night of a night market

lines.text: The night market at Lorong Bayu closed for good last Sunday.
It had run every weekend since forty years, long before the flats around
lines.note: Preposition: 'for' goes with a length of time; 'since' needs a starting point.

lines.text: it were built. On the final evening, hundreds of former customers came to
say goodbye. Mr Tan, who has sold grilled corn there since he was a
lines.note: Tense: the market has closed and the story is in the past, so it is 'had sold'.

lines.text: teenager, gave away his last fifty cobs for free. Some stallholders were cheerful,
so others wept openly as they packed their goods for the last time.
lines.note: Connector: the two groups contrast, so it is 'but'.

lines.text: The close was not caused by falling crowds. The land is needed for
lines.note: Word form: after 'the' a noun is needed here — 'closure'.

lines.text: a new train line that will short many residents’ journeys to work. Few
lines.note: Word form: after 'will' a verb is needed — 'shorten'.

lines.text: people disagree with the plan, yet many feel that something has been lose.
lines.note: Verb form: after 'has been' it is 'lost'.

lines.text: A market is more than a place to shop. It is which neighbours
lines.note: Relative word: a market is a place, so it is 'where'.

lines.text: meet without an appointment and children learn to bargain. Despite the stalls
lines.note: Connector: before a full clause it is 'although'; 'despite' needs a noun.

lines.text: are gone, the smell of grilled corn will stay with us for years.
